openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Tuesday, the day of Mars. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Mars is the old symbol of drive and courage: energy pointed at one target. Breathe square, then aim all of it at the work.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds squares the mind. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then go build.

mindset.body: The Chargers walked into Baltimore without a win this season and left with one. Nobody gave them a reason to believe; they took one. A slow week, a cold pipeline, a quiet launch: none of it is who you are. It's the score before you play. Make the first call, win the first rep, take the first W today. Competitive. Unbeatable. Always rising. fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Tuesday, the day of Mars: run this right after Morning Charge. It's about 32° and clear outside, so keep the RipStick finisher indoors. Mars day means attack every rep.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom's RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time.

Tuesday belongs to Mars. In Hermetic and astrological tradition Mars rules courage, cutting and decisive action. The lesson isn't rage. It's will pointed at a single target until it gives.
The 17th-century German mystic taught that every soul holds a dark fire that becomes light once it's turned toward the good. Your drive isn't the problem. Its direction is the whole game.

'Let one who seeks not stop seeking until one finds. When one finds, one will be troubled; when troubled, astonished; and will reign over all.' The Gnostic path runs straight through discomfort to mastery.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.source: From the wisdom attributed to Solomon
grimoire.body: Solomon wrote: 'For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again' (Proverbs 24:16). Falling isn't the failure. Staying down is. It's the oldest version of fall down 7 stand up 8.

lesson.oneLiner: Great prompts are reusable templates, not one-off magic words.
beats: Open prompts.chat and search for the job you do most: sales emails, landing-page copy, product descriptions.
Read how strong prompts are built: a role, the context, the exact task, and the output format.
Fork one into your own 7EightMade version with your brand voice and the motto baked in.
Save the winners in one place so every drop starts from a proven prompt instead of a blank box.
lesson.takeaway: Steal the structure, add your voice, reuse it forever.
